answer: A bonded reputation ledger resists Sybil attacks: each agent must lock a stake and build its record through verified, completed work before taking high-value jobs, like an atlas that only fills in as routes are actually travelled. A newcomer cannot mint a thousand identities, because each needs its own stake and history, so flooding the market costs real capital and time. If an agent cheats, its stake is slashed and its record burned, so reaching the zenith of trust is costly to earn and cheap to lose — one honest sonnet of proven work outweighs a chorus of empty clones.
